# ui::NativeHost

Header: `winui/render/NativeHost.hpp`.

The interface between a [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol), a leaf wrapping a real Win32 child window such as RichEdit, a shell control or WebView2, and whatever owns the real HWND.

Call it from a [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol). The library implements it, and a test installs TestNativeHost.

Every other control draws itself without a window of its own. [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) hosts what libwinui doesn't reimplement. The control never calls Win32 itself. It calls this interface from [Element::sync_native()](../tree/element.md#sync_native), keyed by its [VisualId](../core/namespace-ui.md#visualid), and the host creates, moves, clips and hides the child window. The window installs its host with Window::set_native_host() (non-owning). The host must outlive every [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) synced against it, since a [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol)'s destructor calls back into it.

Example: 
```cpp
// An app never calls a NativeHost. It puts a NativeControl in the tree, and the window's host
// creates the child window, places it and keeps it in step with the element:
auto edit = std::make_unique<ui::NativeControl>(
    ui::NativeControlDesc{.class_name = "EDIT", .initial_text = "hello"}, ui::Size{100, 20});
window.set_content(std::move(edit));
```

## ~NativeHost

```cpp
virtual ~NativeHost() = default
```

## ensure_created

```cpp
virtual void ensure_created(VisualId id, const NativeControlDesc& desc) = 0
```

Creates the native control for `id` if it doesn't exist yet, and does nothing if it does. A [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) calls this once per sync_native(), whether or not it already has a live handle.

## set_bounds

```cpp
virtual void set_bounds(VisualId id, const Rect& bounds) = 0
```

Moves and resizes the native control to `bounds`, in DIPs like every other [Element](../tree/element.md). The host converts to device pixels.

## set_visible

```cpp
virtual void set_visible(VisualId id, bool visible) = 0
```

Shows or hides the control without destroying its window, for example while it is inactive. Does nothing if `id` has no created control yet.

## destroy

```cpp
virtual void destroy(VisualId id) = 0
```

Destroys the native control. Does nothing if `id` has none.

## set_clip

```cpp
virtual void set_clip(VisualId, const std::optional<Rect>&)
```

Cuts the native control down to `visible` (DIPs, the same space as [set_bounds()](#set_bounds)), or shows all of it for nullopt. A child window ignores the clips the rest of the window is drawn with, so a control half scrolled out of a [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll) would otherwise paint over whatever sits outside the viewport. [NativeControl::sync_native()](../controls/native-control.md#sync_native) sends the part its scrolling ancestors leave in view, through [place()](#place) whenever the control also moved, so a host may keep the region relative to the window. The default does nothing, for a host with nothing to cut.

## place

```cpp
virtual void place(VisualId id, const Rect& bounds, const std::optional<Rect>& visible)
```

Moves the control and clips it in one step, so a host that repaints on a move paints the new position with the new clip, not the one left over from the old position. [NativeControl::sync_native()](../controls/native-control.md#sync_native) calls this whenever the bounds changed; the default is [set_bounds()](#set_bounds) then [set_clip()](#set_clip).

## native_handle

```cpp
virtual NativeHandle native_handle(VisualId id) const = 0
```

The raw platform handle (an HWND on Windows), for control-specific messages a generic [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) can't express, such as WM_SETTEXT or WM_GETTEXT to a RichEdit. nullptr if `id` has no created control yet.

## set_spell_checker

```cpp
void set_spell_checker(SpellChecker* checker)
```

Publishes the window's spell checker, or null when the window has none. Window::sync_native() calls it, and [NativeControl::sync_native()](../controls/native-control.md#sync_native) hands the checker to the control through [Element::sync_spell_checker()](../tree/element.md#sync_spell_checker).

Other controls get the checker when they take focus. A [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) never becomes the window's focused element, because keyboard focus inside it belongs to the child window, so it gets the checker through this sync pass instead.

## spell_checker

```cpp
SpellChecker* spell_checker() const
```

The checker [set_spell_checker()](#set_spell_checker) last published, or null. Non-owning.

## begin_sync

```cpp
void begin_sync()
```

Window::sync_native() brackets its tree walk with these. Every [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) the walk reaches reports through [present()](#present) whether it should show. [end_sync()](#end_sync) then hides every control the walk didn't reach, such as one on a [Tabs](../controls/tabs.md#uitabs) page or [NavigationShell](../controls/navigation-shell.md#uinavigationshell) entry that isn't selected, and [present()](#present) shows it again the next time a pass reaches it. Only [end_sync()](#end_sync) hides anything, so a host whose controls are synced directly never hides one this way. This one starts a pass.

## end_sync

```cpp
void end_sync()
```

Ends a pass: hides (set_visible(false)) every shown control [present()](#present) wasn't called for since [begin_sync()](#begin_sync).

## present

```cpp
void present(VisualId id, bool visible)
```

Called by [NativeControl::sync_native()](../controls/native-control.md#sync_native) on every sync: `visible` is whether any of the control shows. Calls [set_visible()](#set_visible) only on a change; a control starts out shown.

## presented

```cpp
bool presented(VisualId id) const
```

Whether [present()](#present)/end_sync() last left the control shown (true for one never presented).

## forget

```cpp
void forget(VisualId id)
```

Drops the control's presence record; [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol)'s destructor calls it before [destroy()](#destroy).

## notify_host_lost

```cpp
static void notify_host_lost(NativeControl& control) noexcept
```

Tells `control`, a [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) registered through [set_owner()](#set_owner), that this host is going away while it lives on (its window was closed; the app still owns the [Window](../tree/window.md) and its tree). The control forgets the host and its native window, and gets a new one from the next sync_native(). A host calls it from its destructor for every owner still registered.

## set_owner

```cpp
virtual void set_owner(VisualId, NativeControl*)
```

Records which [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) owns `id`, so a host that receives platform events addressed to the child window can route them back to its element. On Windows that is a child window's WM_CONTEXTMENU: a right-click inside a native control goes to the child window and never reaches Window::handle_context_menu(), so the host looks the owner up by its handle and calls [Element::handle_context_menu()](../tree/element.md#handle_context_menu) on it directly.

[NativeControl::sync_native()](../controls/native-control.md#sync_native) calls it right after [ensure_created()](#ensure_created), so the owner is registered for exactly as long as the control exists. [destroy()](#destroy) drops it again, and [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) is non-movable, so the pointer can't go stale. The default does nothing, for a host with no platform events to route. A host implements it, and only [NativeControl](../controls/native-control.md#uinativecontrol) calls it.
